title: Pruning doesn't stop oneshot quadlet units
body:
### Issue Description

Pruning (`podman system prune`, `podman network prune`, etc.) deletes the resources (network, etc.) without stopping the relevant quadlet systemd units. Subsequently, systemd will believe that resource is still active and proceed to dependents, which will fail as the dependency isn't really active.

A typical setup is a scheduled oneshot container with it's own network, combined with a scheduled pruning job. Pruning will delete the network while leaving the network quadlet unit active (because it's a `Type=oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit=yes`). On the next scheduled start, systemd will believe the network is still active and start the container right away, while the container will fail as the network doesn't actually exist.

A workaround is to make the dependency resource to have `StopWhenUnneeded=yes` under `[Unit]`, if all dependencies are managed by systemd.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Configure with quadlet a oneshot container and its own network with `Network=foo.network`.
1. `systemctl start <container-unit>`
1. At this point, container unit is dead while the network unit remains active.
1. `podman network prune`
1. `systemctl start <container-unit>`

### Describe the results you received

- After `podman network prune`, the network is deleted while the network unit remains active.
- After `systemctl start <container-unit>`, container startup fails due to missing network.

### Describe the results you expected

- After `podman network prune`, the network is deleted and the network unit becomes dead.
- After `systemctl start <container-unit>`, container starts successfully.

Alternatively, there should be a separate quadlet-aware mechanism to prune resources.
